harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, created user datauser and a dedicated loop-mounted XFS filesystem (/srv/img/data-quota.img) mounted at /srv/data with the usrquota option, then set an XFS user quota (bsoft=bhard=100m) for datauser via xfs_quota. Persisted the mount in /etc/fstab. Verified filesystem-level enforcement both before and after a full node restart: writes up to 100MB succeed, writes beyond 100MB are rejected by the kernel with "Disk quota exceeded". Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id (809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799), issued a non-blocking shutdown -r now, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id (89834fbd-ce98-4d4d-804f-60fa9caa8bb1) and new uptime -s (2026-09-29 vs prior 2026-08-26), and re-verified the quota mount, quota limits, and live enforcement recovered automatically via fstab.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/filesystem (RHEL 7.9, root fs XFS with no quota mount options, no existing /srv/data)
Confirmed xfs_quota binary already present at /usr/sbin/xfs_quota (no yum repo access to install packages)
Created system account datauser
Created 512MB backing image /srv/img/data-quota.img, formatted as XFS
Mounted the image at /srv/data via loop device with usrquota option; chowned /srv/data to datauser
Set XFS user quota bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser via xfs_quota -x limit
Added persistent fstab entry (loop,uquota) and verified umount/mount -a re-establishes the quota mount
Tested enforcement pre-restart: 50MB write succeeded, subsequent write hit Disk quota exceeded at 100MB used; cleaned up test files
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and healthy quota state
Issued non-blocking reboot (shutdown -r now backgrounded), polled node1 until reachable again
Confirmed changed boot_id and new uptime -s proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified quota mount, quota limits, and live 100MB enforcement post-restart

evidence.summary: useradd datauser succeeded; id shows uid=1001(datauser)

evidence.requirement: /srv/data is a filesystem-enforced 100MB quota for datauser
evidence.summary: Created and formatted loop-backed XFS image, mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, set bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser via xfs_quota

evidence.requirement: Quota is enforced by the filesystem itself, not just configured
evidence.summary: 50MB write as datauser succeeded; subsequent write failed with kernel-level 'Disk quota exceeded' at exactly 100M used
umount + mount -a from fstab re-established usrquota mount and 100M limits

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline / boot identity for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799 and confirmed /srv/data quota mount healthy before restart
Issued backgrounded shutdown -r now (ack returned), observed connection timeout mid-reboot, then reconnected successfully

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: New boot_id 89834fbd-ce98-4d4d-804f-60fa9caa8bb1 and new uptime -s (2026-09-29 10:25:31) differ from pre-restart values
After restart, /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab with usrquota and 100M limits intact; live write test again rejected at exactly 100MB with Disk quota exceeded
